checks: New conversations retain native creation/first-turn acknowledgement separation and partial-thread unknown recovery. Listing overlay bridges native indexing lag without substituting for persisted pagination.

Loaded existing conversations permit same-provider models and known aliases, while turn/start and resume refuse provider changes. Disabled original providers must be restored before the supported loaded-idle conversion.

Conversion creates a native independent paginated target. Target native header and new session identity are preserved; source nonheader records are historical copied data. No native fork, parent reference, hardlink or source history_base is introduced.

After native source close/flush, one stable source witness is held throughout copy. Helper reads source only and publishes atomically to the distinct empty target. Repair, settings, model/provider and title changes only address the new target.

The real CLI regression asserts new sessionId/header session_id, null parent/fork/history_base, distinct path/inode, original provider/title/raw witness preservation after close, original deletion followed by target cold restart and continuation.

No model input is dispatched by conversion. Original source and new target pending admission cover resume/turn races; positive ACK or post-write failures remain unknown with distinct partial target identity, never automatic resubmission.

Original and converted threads keep independent persisted conversation identity and runtime history-completeness state. Same project/cwd/environment and execution settings are verified; public compacted replacement history, tool pairs and public summary remain represented.

Ordinary native archive/unarchive/name requests remain their existing explicit operations, not hidden conversion stages. Source title is not renamed by conversion. Explicit user modifications are separate operations from source preservation evidence.

Disconnect revokes connection-scoped history and subsystem leases; fatal native epochs clear cached sessions and retain unknown activity. History pages and automatic load use revision/continuation checks rather than starting a new prompt.

Queue and goal mutations retain thread identity, history and user-provenance checks; automatic loading refuses active persisted continuation without acknowledgement. Conversion rejects active goal/queue, and does not copy their independent live database state.

Native ancestor agent listing has its own cross-provider semantics; the earlier suspected missing filter was disproved by official implementation and a real two-provider agent fixture. No unnecessary production parameter was retained.
No additional product defect was established in this scoped self-check. The four JS CI repairs are fixture-only and separately independently reviewed.
limits: The conversion implementation is authored by this reviewer; this report cannot replace the independent root, helper/runtime and deployment reviews cited above.

Source byte immutability begins after normal native close/flush. This does not assert every raw byte or native indexing timestamp is unchanged between pre-close and post-close; no conversion is applied to original provider, title or conversation payload.

Independent conversations share their selected project filesystem and external services; copying history does not undo tool effects. Historical tool/agent IDs remain records, not newly running agents or copied ownership.

Independent plain paginated histories and supported compacted replacement are covered. Inherited/opaque-provider compaction/unsupported compressed disk formats are rejected rather than silently reconstructed.

No additional Linux JavaScript test environment was created. Fixed Linux test results are still pending the next exact-head full CI; existing targeted 29 distinct Windows cases and final native identity case are evidence, not a full gate.
CI1 remains failed, including refused aggregate coverage. CI2 has not been observed or declared passed by this report.
